sections.h2: Who values and bills a house in Paterson?
sections.html:
In Paterson the Tax Assessor's Office values every parcel, and the city's tax collector sends the bill. The assessor appraises land and buildings under state statute, keeps ownership and transfer records current, checks building permits and maintains values. The same office approves veteran, senior and disabled deductions and puts together the added and omitted assessment list.

The assessor's office is in City Hall, 155 Market Street, with weekday counter hours that end at 4:30 p.m. Assessment appeals go to the Passaic County Board of Taxation in Totowa, and the assessor represents the city at those hearings and in New Jersey Tax Court. For a due date or a payoff amount on a specific parcel, ask the Paterson tax collector at City Hall for the figure in writing.

Paterson is the biggest city in Passaic County and a tightly packed one, with 161,793 residents in 2025 on 8.41 square miles of land. For 2020 to 2024 a typical owned home was valued at $360,100, typical rent was $1,548 and typical household income was $55,997. Only 26.9% of housing is owner-occupied, so many sellers are small landlords with two-, three- or four-family houses.

The city has 49,865 households averaging 3.15 people. Because 67.3% of residents age 5 and over speak a language other than English at home, listing materials in more than one language can reach more buyers. Interstate 80 runs through the city and the Garden State Parkway passes its southern edge.

sections.h2: Appeal deadlines and how to file
sections.html:
Paterson was the town that revalued or reassessed for 2026, which pushed its appeal cutoff to May 1 that year. The same pattern applies after any later citywide revaluation.

  • A regular appeal reaches the county board by April 1, or 45 days after the notices were bulk mailed if that comes later.
  • Assessments above $1,000,000 can skip the board and be filed in state Tax Court.
  • Added and omitted assessments are appealed before December 1.
  • A board judgment can be carried to Tax Court inside 45 days.

Do not file until the assessment card has arrived, which is after February 1. After a revaluation, assessments are meant to equal market value as of the prior October 1, so recent Paterson sales before that date are the best evidence. Added or omitted assessment bills are generally sent in October and payable November 1.

The city offers three local benefits, each applied for through the assessor with a claim form. The deductions reduce the bill for qualified owners, and the exemption removes it for a narrow group.

Paterson deductions and exemptions, with eligibility and claim form
BenefitAmountMain eligibility testClaim form
Veteran or surviving spouse deduction$250 a yearOwner and New Jersey resident on October 1 of the pre-tax year; qualifying wartime or peacekeeping serviceV.S.S.
Senior, disabled or surviving spouse deduction$250 a yearAge 65 or older, or permanently disabled, as of December 31; income under $10,000 excluding certain benefitsPTD
Disabled veteran exemptionFull exemption of home and lotCertified 100% permanently and totally disabled by the VA; owner and residentD.V.S.S.E.

Veteran applicants need a copy of the DD-214, and the veteran and senior claim forms can be filed with either the assessor or the collector. The disabled veteran claim can be filed at any time of year. State programs such as ANCHOR and Senior Freeze are separate, so call the Division of Taxation for their filing window.

sections.h2: What happens if Paterson property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Paterson sells unpaid tax liens at an online auction on the city's New Jersey tax sale site. Parcel lists, delinquency amounts and costs are free to view, and bidding follows the instructions posted there.

State law allows an accelerated sale when taxes or liens are still open on the 11th day of the eleventh month of the fiscal year. The city fixes its own late interest inside the state ceiling and may allow ten days of grace. An owner who misses a first quarter installment should call the collector early, since interest starts on the due date and each skipped quarter adds to the debt.

A tax sale certificate is a recorded claim against the parcel, and a seller must redeem or cancel it before title is clear.

  • Request a payoff letter that covers the closing date.
  • Ask the Passaic County Clerk whether any tax sale certificate is on record.
  • Redeem the certificate before closing so title is clear.

sections.h2: What else should a Paterson seller check before listing?
sections.html:
Ask the city for open permits and violations before you list. After Hurricane Irene in August 2011 the Passaic River rose to levels unseen for a century, so buyers may ask about past water in basements. The Paterson School District covers all the area inside the city limits.

Recording happens at the Passaic County Clerk, whose fee schedule also carries the realty transfer tax table by price band. Because the assessor keeps transfer records, the tax roll changes owners once the deed is recorded.

Once you have a contract, the sequence is short. The closing agent orders the payoff letter from the tax collector, searches for any tax sale certificate, and confirms that permits are closed. The balance and any certificate are paid from the seller's proceeds, the deed goes to the county clerk, and the assessor updates the roll after recording.

Landlords with tenants should also pull copies of leases, since a buyer will want to see what comes with the building. A cash buyer purchasing as-is will not ask for repairs or wait on a lender, but the tax payoff and recording steps are the same, so ordering the payoff letter early is the best way to protect the closing date.

faqs.q: Where is the Paterson Tax Assessor's Office?
faqs.a: City Hall, 155 Market Street, Paterson. Weekday hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: What is the Paterson appeal deadline?
faqs.a: April 1 for a regular appeal. After a citywide revaluation or reassessment, as in 2026, the deadline moves to May 1.

faqs.q: How much is the Paterson veteran property tax deduction?
faqs.a: The deduction is $250 a year for a qualified veteran or surviving spouse who owns the home and was a New Jersey resident on the prior October 1. A veteran rated 100% permanently and totally disabled by the VA may qualify for a complete exemption instead.
Yes, in an online auction. Parcel details are posted on the city's New Jersey tax sale page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Paterson house that owes property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The closing agent settles the arrears from the seller's proceeds. First get a payoff letter from the Paterson tax collector, and clear any tax sale certificate before closing.
